A1.justification: Despite the changed title and format, both PDFs describe the same GKAN-ODE study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original neural-model, symbolic-recovery and trajectory-prediction experiments on four synthetic dynamical systems and COVID-19, H1N1 and SARS data.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds topology-agnostic comparisons, denoising and derivative-estimation experiments, additional metrics and training analyses.

M1.justification: The core GKAN-ODE architecture, multiplicative nodes and GP/Spline-Wise distillation procedures remain. Appendix C.6 adds an evaluated pipeline variant using cubic-polynomial smoothing before derivative estimation, a limited procedural extension. Most expanded method descriptions explain existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use KUR, EPID, BIO and POP synthetic dynamics, the same graph families and observational-noise levels, and COVID-19, H1N1 and SARS data. The new analyses vary models, metrics and preprocessing within retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds topology-agnostic MLP-ODE and MLP-ODE+GP comparisons in Appendix C.5 and includes TPSINDy in the parameter-count comparison. The principal graph-aware comparators remain. OSW names the original KAN fitting algorithm already evaluated in v1, rather than a new baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds MSE, RMSE and MAPE evaluation, central-finite-difference testing and cubic-smoothing protocols. Section 4.3 describes epidemic formula selection using validation data extracted from training data, replacing v1's selection on training data itself; rerunning is not established. The main synthetic splits and OOD evaluation design remain.

E4.justification: Appendices C.1–C.2 and C.5–C.8 substantially extend diagnostic evidence: temporal error growth, metric sensitivity, topology dependence, denoising, derivative-estimator sensitivity and training/validation convergence. The multiplicative-node and original-Spline-Wise comparisons were already present in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across three OOD test graphs and refer to generation seeds in the codebase. Additional tables extend this reporting practice; no increased training-run count, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results through the alternative-metric tables, topology-agnostic formulas, denoising experiment and diagnostic curves. For example, Table 18 newly reports denoised BIO errors at 20 dB of 3.45e-3 for GKAN-ODE+GP and 8.90e-2 for TPSINDy. The principal learned symbolic coefficients are retained; these additions do not establish same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The written training-loss normalization changes from 1/(NT) in v1 Equation 4 to 1/[N(T+1)] in v2 Equation 6, matching the inclusive time sum. The pruning example's unpruned operation count is corrected from two to four. Existing KAN representation and sparsity mathematics are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds the evaluation pipeline and adds an explicit claim of up to two orders of magnitude lower OOD trajectory error. Equation recovery, graph generalization, parameter efficiency and the GKAN-ODE/Spline-Wise contributions were already claimed in v1, so the central contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands explanations of why multiplicative nodes help Spline-Wise extraction, topology-agnostic failures, denoising and accuracy–complexity tradeoffs. It adds explicit limitations concerning static topology, autonomous dynamics, scalar states and noisy derivatives. Some new interpretations overreach: Appendix C.2 claims universal metric superiority although Tables 12–14 favor TPSINDy on KUR.

D1.justification: V2 supplies important missing details: Adam optimization, 1000 epochs and early-stopping patience, derivative boundary handling, rollout solver and tolerances, explicit symbolic operator libraries, and validation/test trajectory lengths. It newly documents TPSINDy coefficient refitting on the first 90% of observations and changes the cloud-instance label. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds references covering graph neural ODEs, alternative KAN parameterizations and polynomial denoising, and sharpens comparisons of expressivity, interpretability and prior evaluation practices. The main positioning of GKAN-ODE relative to LLC, TPSINDy and earlier KAN work remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, its abstract rewritten, and its methodological explanations substantially expanded. Numbered sections and organized appendices replace the earlier structure; KAN background moves into related work, OOD evaluation moves into Methods, and a dedicated limitations discussion is added.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the watermarked two-column layout with a single-column format, adds positioning and pipeline diagrams, expands architecture illustrations, and introduces several diagnostic plots and tables. Earlier performance figures are merged, equation tables reorganized, and existing noise and epidemic plots relocated into the main text.

improvement.justification: The added controls, reproducibility details and explicit limitations improve scrutiny of the existing findings. The net gain is tempered by overstated new summaries: Appendix C.2 claims wins on every system, although Tables 12–14 show lower KUR errors for TPSINDy. V2 provides more useful supporting evidence, but these inconsistencies limit the improvement in scientific reliability.
